## Python bindings and type stubs (`pyharp` module, `python/*.pyi`) {#sec-ch10-bindings}

### Summary

pyharp's options are C++ structs; pybind11 code in `python/csrc` exposes them to Python, and hand-written stub
files (`python/*.pyi`) describe them to editors and type checkers. Nothing generates the bindings or the stubs from
the structs, so the three can drift apart. This section compares them option by option at the pin.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Which C++ options a Python user can set, and which the stubs declare.

**Data.** 9 option structs, 58 options and flag accessors; the installed `pyharp` module; `python/*.pyi`.

**Placement.** Import of `pyharp` (bindings); static analysis (stubs).

**Activation.** Always.

**Guarantee / limits.** 16 options have no binding and 29 no stub (Tests layer); none is checked by CI.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-bindings.
:::

Local symbols: none.

An option missing from the bindings can be set only through YAML or C++; one missing from the stubs works but is
invisible to type checkers and editor completion.

### Derivation

None: this section compares interfaces and has no equations.

### Numerical method

Each option of a struct is declared with the macro `ADD_ARG(type, name)`, which generates a getter and a setter of
that name; some solver structs add boolean accessors that test a comma-separated `flags` string
(`ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl`, {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl repo=pyharp >}}). The
bindings expose an option by naming it once more with the macro `ADD_OPTION` of `python/csrc/pyoptions.hpp`, for
example in `bind_rtsolver` ({{< code python/csrc/pyrtsolver.cpp bind_rtsolver repo=pyharp >}}); the stubs declare
it again as a `def` in `python/pyharp.pyi` ({{< code python/pyharp.pyi repo=pyharp >}}). The check
`bindings_diff.py` reads every `ADD_ARG` and flag accessor under `src/`, looks each up as an attribute of the
installed Python class, and as a `def` under the class of the same name in the stubs.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Toon options | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl repo=pyharp >}} | `ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl` | always |
| Toon bindings | {{< code python/csrc/pyrtsolver.cpp bind_rtsolver repo=pyharp >}} | `bind_rtsolver` | always |
| module entry | {{< code python/csrc/pyharp.cpp PYBIND11_MODULE repo=pyharp >}} | `PYBIND11_MODULE` | always |
| stubs | {{< code python/pyharp.pyi repo=pyharp >}} | file | always |

: Code map of the bindings. {#tbl-ch10-bindings-code}

1. `PYBIND11_MODULE` ({{< code python/csrc/pyharp.cpp PYBIND11_MODULE repo=pyharp >}}) calls `bind_opacity`,
   `bind_radiation`, `bind_math`, `bind_constants`, `bind_integrator` and `bind_rtsolver`.
2. `bind_rtsolver` ({{< code python/csrc/pyrtsolver.cpp bind_rtsolver repo=pyharp >}}) binds
   `wave_lower`, `wave_upper`, `flags` and `top_emission_flag` of `ToonMcKay89Options`, and the read-only flag
   accessors; it does not bind `btop_factor`.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bindings_diff.py` `[B1]`-`[B3]` | each C++ option has a binding and a stub | 0 missing | outline target |
| `tests/test_opacity_options.py` | `OpacityOptions` round trip from Python | exact | test's choice |

: Checks of the bindings. {#tbl-ch10-bindings-tests}

The comparison finds 16 options with no binding and 29 with no stub declaration[^ch10-bind]:

- `ToonMcKay89Options`: `btop_factor` is not bound (YAML only); none of its 9 options appears in any stub, and the
  stubs declare neither `ToonMcKay89` nor `ToonMcKay89Options`.
- `IntegratorOptions`: `verbose` is not bound; 5 of 7 options are missing from the stubs.
- `RadiationBandOptions`: the `toon` option is missing from the stubs.
- `RadiationModelOptions` (9 options) has no Python class; `Layer2LevelOptions` (4) and `BeerLambertOptions` (1)
  have none either. `BeerLambertOptions` belongs to a solver whose source file is not compiled.
- `OpacityOptions`, `RadiationOptions` and `IntegratorWeight` are complete in both.

The comparison runs against the installed module of each source build and gives the same lines for both pydisort
versions. The outline's target, zero missing, is not met.

### Limits

- **Binding and stub gaps (CANDIDATE, Python interface).** 16 options are not settable from Python and 29 are not
  declared in the stubs[^ch10-bind]; no test or CI step compares the three.
- **Method coverage.** The comparison covers options (`ADD_ARG` and flag accessors) only, not methods, functions or
  the shapes of `forward`; those are not compared here.
